issue_context.title: Allow setting the Activity properties after Activity creation and before starting it when using ActivitySource

I don't think it is intended to support all possible scenario in ActivitySource in first version. Your scenario can be considered in the future releases. You still have the option to use old way of creating the Activity and using DiagnosticSource. This still work.

For tags allocation, you can still avoid the allocation before creating the activity by setting `ActivityCreationOptions.SamplingTags` in the listener callbacks. This will still allocate at that time but for sure it will be determined the Activity is going to be allocated anyway.

It is too late to change any APIs in the 5.0 release.

>  You still have the option to use old way of creating the `Activity `and using `DiagnosticSource`. This still work.

From the perspective of a telemetry producer - yes. But a producer does not know whether this scenario is important for any actual consumer. And if a producer who followed the existing guidance wants to transition to the "new way" while enabling all previous scenarios, they cannot. I completely realize the current spot in the release cycle, but if this item was to be tracked for prioritization in the next cycles, then, for the record, I think that the workaround you mention does not apply. :)

> For tags allocation, you can still avoid the allocation before creating the activity by setting `ActivityCreationOptions.SamplingTags` in the listener callbacks. 

Thanks for pointing it out. I had missed the existence of that property. However, having had a look at it, I do not fully understand its use. Is there a doc or an example? What I mean above is that when invoking `ActivitySource.StartActivity(..)` you need to pass an `IEnumerable` object on the heap. So the allocation will occur when creating that object while the sampling decision is taken within the scope of the `ActivitySource.StartActivity(..)` method. So regardless of whether or not you decided to allocate the activity, you will have to allocate the tags collection object.

Please let me know if you guys consider these Activity-related submissions as a valuable input for forward-looking planning / for the next cycle. I do not want to create a distraction if it is not productive. :)

Thanks!

> if a producer who followed the existing guidance wants to transition to the "new way" while enabling all previous scenarios, they cannot.

Agree. What i was trying to say is, this is not supported scenario yet with ActivitySource. I was pointing if someone blocked for now can consider use the old way.

For `ActivityCreationOptions.SamplingTags`, the idea is when you are calling `ActivitySource.StartActivity` you'll not pass any tags at that time but in the listener you'll have a chance to add the tags during then. I am not sure if this will fully satisfy your scenario. you may look at our test https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e2e43f44f1032780fa7c2bb965153c9da615c3d0/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource/tests/ActivitySourceTests.cs#L605 which show how it is used.

If the allocation is very critical to your scenario, you may consider having IEnumerable thread local object (e.g. List<>) which you can use for all subsequent calls on same thread. The allocation would be once per thread instead to be ones per ActivityStart call.

> Agree. What i was trying to say is, this is not supported scenario yet with ActivitySource. I was pointing if someone blocked for now can consider use the old way.

Gotcha, thanks!

> For ActivityCreationOptions.SamplingTags, the idea is when you are calling ActivitySource.StartActivity you'll not pass any tags at that time but in the listener you'll have a chance to add the tags during then.

Ah, understood. This is a different scenario. I was talking about saving the allocation that is only required only to pass parameters to StartActivity(..) 

> If the allocation is very critical to your scenario, you may consider having IEnumerable thread local object (e.g. List<>) which you can use for all subsequent calls on same thread. 

That might work, but the complexity of implementing such cache and the perf overhead required for cleaning it before each use make this feel concerning. Of course, .NET5 is done. I would love a performance-focused overload similar to what I mentioned above to be considered for the next release.

If the team decides that such an overload is beneficial, I'd be happy to contribute when the time comes. :)

Thanks!

> StartActivity(..) overloads that have parameters like string tag1Key, string tag1Value, ... for the first few tags.

This sounds like a good improvement. In most cases the number of initial tags/attributes is very low (or none). More tags are added after actually creating the activity and knowing the sampling decision.
``` 
(if activity != null && activity.IsAllDataRequested == true) 
{
  add tags.
}
```

Thanks @macrogreg!

> System.Diagnostics.ActivitySource.StartActivity(..) is missing an overload that takes Baggage items

StartActivity() was intended to take the minimum amount of data necessary for sampling. Adding more types of data trades off performance for more flexibility in sampling and richer data available on the start callback. Another direction is to create an API that returns an unstarted Activity allowing Start() to be decoupled from sampling. That option is trading off more complicated API usage for richer data available on the start callback. I'm not opposed to this in principle, but they first hurdle to clear would be to understand why do we need specific data attached to a Start callback if that same data will be available later in the Stop callback? 

> However, this will require that an enumerable is allocated before StartActivity(..) is called

We added the overload which took tags because OpenTelemetry defined that it must be possible to give tags to the sampling algorithm. My hope is that in practice it is a rare case that the sampling algorithm needs to consider tags because doing so implies you are paying perf costs to generate them and analyze them even for sampled-out activities. The higher performing route would be to determine in advance that the tags aren't relevant for sampling and provide them only after an Activity has been sampled in using Activity.SetTag(). If there is a need for higher performance scenarios where certain tags are available to the sampler or available in the Start() callback I'm not opposed to optimizations you suggested, but I'd like to be able to tie to some specific customer or use-case that the work is improving.

> I'm not opposed to this in principle, but they first hurdle to clear would be to understand why do we need specific data attached to a Start callback if that same data will be available later in the Stop callback?

Agree. At this point I am merely pointing out that the [.NET guidance pre .NET 5](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource/src/ActivityUserGuide.md#starting-and-stopping-activity) was to include baggage for the Activity Start callback and the new API doe snot allow it. We may decide that the guidance was wrong or that the different ins not important and does not justify more complexity. Both is OK. Just feels like it should be an explicit decision, rather than an oversight. :)

> We added the overload which took tags because OpenTelemetry defined that it must be possible to give tags to the sampling algorithm. My hope is that in practice it is a rare case that the sampling algorithm needs to consider tags because doing so implies you are paying perf costs to generate them and analyze them even for sampled-out activities. The higher performing route would be to determine in advance that the tags aren't relevant for sampling and provide them only after an Activity has been sampled in using Activity.SetTag(). If there is a need for higher performance scenarios where certain tags are available to the sampler or available in the Start() callback I'm not opposed to optimizations you suggested, but I'd like to be able to tie to some specific customer or use-case that the work is improving.

Ok, that makes sense. However, in the context of the aforementioned old-API-guidance, it was not clear to me that the purpose of the overload that takes tags was to make tags available to the sampler, not the Start event handler.

I think others may also be confuted in a similar manner. Perhaps we can add guidance to the docs to say something along the lines that the recommended pattern is to:

* Only include info into the StartActivity(..) that is relevant for sampling
* Start event handlers should _not_ expect that the information that is logically available at the beginning of the operation represented by an Activity is actually attached to the Activity when the Start event is raised. (E.g., input parameters).
* Both should be attached to the Activity when the End event is raised:
   * tracing-relevant information that is readily available _at the beginning_ of the sub-operation represented by an Activity (e.g. input parameters)
   * as well as tracing-relevant information that is only available _at the end_ of the sub-operation represented by an Activity (e.g. results) 
* This is different from previously published DiagnosticSource examples, where the input parameters relevant information was passed to the start event

That would clear things up. :)
Note, however, this would prevent scenarios where an exporter wishes to record as useful events as possible both, at the start and the end of an Activity.

> That would clear things up. :)

Agreed. This matches guidance I had in mind but we hadn't explicitly documented it as far as I know. I created https://github.com/dotnet/docs/issues/20825 to track doing that.

> [.NET guidance pre .NET 5](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource/src/ActivityUserGuide.md#starting-and-stopping-activity)

Yeah I consider that guidance out-of-date now. Perhaps we should use this issue to track deprecating that info and redirecting it to the official docs once we've got that complete?

This works from my perspective. To inform this whole thing, here is a curious piece of historical trivia.

I was not involved into the creation of Activity class, but if I understand correctly (I would be curious to learn for sure), it was inspired by a an internal logging library that were used by some Application Insights backed services. Or perhaps it was not, but the APIs look similar and there is some overlap in the people involved, so who knows. :)

That other library already operated with the term Activity, but the focus was more around structured logging, rather than distributed context. You started and finished Activities to describe sub-operations of your business logic. You could also attach properties (=tags) to the Activities. The system flew the Current activity across async boundaries, in 4.5 - using a custom synchronization context; later - using AsyncLocal. A guy named Bogdan and another guy called Greg created that system in 2013/14. Not sure if you know Bogdan. Greg is pleased to have this conversation with you. :)

The activities were written to a configurable sink. Back then is was a file or an early re-incarnation of MDS. Later, it was Application Insights. We had to decide, at what point would we record a persistent event:
- when as activity is completed?
- every time a property is changed?
.. this was changed many times and was made configurable, but in the end most services adopted a model where a record was emitted at the start and at the end of each activity, where the information available at the start (e.g. input parameters) was included into the start record. The reason for that was that it was very useful to do log-based debugging in case of service issues: you could trace the execution flow by reading activity events and if a problem occurred during an activity, you still had a record of it starting with all the relevant info.

The reason I am dwelling in this is because I believe that over time, the systems we build may evolve so that these scenarios may move into focus again.

.NET Activities are not used for structured logging today (I mean structured as in business-logic structure of the app, not structure of a log entry). Instead, they are focused on understanding the distributed flow and on propagating distributed tracing context. For that - indeed - I cannot think of why it would be necessary to persist an activity started event. However, as I envision the future, I cannot help the feeling that logging and tracing want to be One thing. 
Could it be that in a few years we will arrive at a spot where the ILogger just adds events (tags, properties) onto the current activity? Or perhaps, in a reversed scenario, a tracing backend will be the same as a logging backend with ActivityStartEvent, InformationalLogEvent, ActivityEndEvent, ErrorLogEvent, etc., just being different values in the Kind column of an all-encompassing application log stream?

So, yes, thinking of the scenarios of this year's release, there is no need to any information to the activity before it starts, beyond what is required for sampling. The API for .NET 5 is done and its a good one.

But going forward, allowing the exporter to log full-fidelity activity-start events, and encouraging telemetry producers to emit telemetry in a way that makes it possible may lead to a more flexible and powerful telemetry platform. Just my 5 cents. :)

Moving the original description added by @macrogreg here for the record as we need to modify the description up to match what have discussed and decided on. 

*@macrogreg original description*

I think there is a scenario supported by the pre-.NET-5 Activity APIs based on `DiagnosticSource` that is not supported in the new `ActivitySource` based APIs:

**`System.Diagnostics.ActivitySource.StartActivity(..)` is missing an overload that takes Baggage items.**

Consider .NET's own guidance on using `Activity` with `DiagnosticSource`:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource/src/ActivityUserGuide.md#starting-and-stopping-activity

In this scenario, a telemetry consumer who chooses to listen to `"Http_In"`-evens will receive _Start_ and _Stop_ events such that the _Start_ events already contain information from the `"Correlation-Context"`-headers in the `Baggage` bag attached to the activity. (In addition, the whole `HttpContext context` object is also passed, but this is not the focus here.)

On contrary, in the new `ActivitySource`-based APIs, the listeners are notified within the scope of the `ActivitySource.StartActivity(..)` method. The creator of the activity only receives a reference to the new activity after the potentially registered listeners have been notified and finished processing the _Start_ event. Only information that can be passed as arguments to the `StartActivity(..)` method can reach the listeners.

So the scenario that is used as the "model" scenario in .NET's own docs is not supported.

_If we consider this to indeed be a problem worth addressing, we should not stop at `Baggage` and consider that it applies to <ins>all</ins> _Activity_ properties that existed pre-.NET-5 and were settable on an `Activity` instance before is is passed to `DiagnosticSource.StartActivity(..)`._

I realized how late to the final release the product is. There are several possible approaches:

* I am missing something, and there is a workaround already (I hope for this to be the case :) ). Perhaps we can include it into some doc.

* We decide that this is indeed a problem, but we are too late in the cycle to fix it. The we should still acknowledge and document it, and track for a future release.

* We consider it fixing for .NET 5. If so, please let me know, I'd be happy to prepare a PR.

Thanks for considering this!

-----------

**(Update an hour later)** Just discovered an additional (related) issue, adding relevant info here:

For convenience, here is the current [ActivitySource public surface](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/92180ed3e98bd6153124d6a80095cefa31267711/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource/ref/System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSourceActivity.cs#L131).

The `Tags` of an `Activity` are not exactly affected by the above problem as `ActivitySource.StartActivity(..)` has overloads that take an `IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, object>> tags` parameter. However, this will require that an enumerable is allocated before `StartActivity(..)` is called. This is problematic in two ways. One of them is easier to address than the other:

1. If the activity would _not_ be created due to sampling (i.e. `StartActivity(..)` returns `null`), then the allocation of the enumerable and _all_ its members was for nothing. This is _hard_ to address in the current model. At this stage all we can do is to document it and recommend a best way to minimize overhead.

2. Even if the Activity object _is_ created, there is still an allocation if the _IEnumerable_ just to pass parameters. The object will likely not survive beyond Gen0, but still: so much work was done to avoid allocations, that it seems weird. This could be addressed by providing `StartActivity(..)` overloads that have parameters like `string tag1Key`, `string tag1Value`, ... for the first few tags. This could help skipping that allocation for the common case where there is just a few tags. Notably, having tags and/or baggage is likely much more frequent than having links, events etc. So yes, the number of overloads would grow, but would not explode uncontrollably. :)
